name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
description: VoiceAssistant-Eval is a comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, and spoken dialogue for listening; multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and various scenarios for speaking; and highly heterogeneous images for viewing. The benchmark evaluates 21 open-source models and GPT-4o-Audio, measuring the quality of response content and speech, as well as their consistency.
creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li (CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK)
citeAs: Wang, K., Ren, H., Lu, Z., Zhan, M., & Li, H. (2025). VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants Across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing. arXiv:2509.22651v1 [cs.CL].
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from 37 existing datasets spanning natural sounds, music, dialogue, and various images. For voice personalization evaluation, texts from RoleBench were used, with 100 distinct roles selected and three representative audio clips collected per role. Text instructions were converted to audio using three TTS models (F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B). The Listening subset draws from 23 audio understanding datasets, the Speaking subset from 22 datasets (11 text and 11 audio), and the Viewing subset from MMMU spanning 30 disciplines and 30 image formats.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Approximately 10% of candidates were removed during the validation stage due to corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and demonstrably incorrect answers.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data was extracted from 37 existing datasets including LibriSpeech, Common Voice, Clotho, AudioCaps, AVQA, MusicCaps, MUSIC-AVQA, MMMU, RoleBench, VocalBench, VoiceBench, SD-Eval, AIR-Bench, and many others spanning audio (speech, sound, music) and visual modalities.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text instructions were preprocessed for TTS synthesis: special image reference tokens were replaced with descriptive phrases, text was rewritten using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct to handle numbers and mathematical expressions, and multiple-choice options were rephrased for readability. Speech was synthesized using F5-TTS, ChatTTS, and Dia-1.6B, evaluated with UTMOS Strong (threshold 3.8), and transcribed with Whisper-Large-v3; only audio with the lowest word error rate was retained. In total, 13,471 high-quality speech audio files were synthesized.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A four-stage curation process was applied: (1) Deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance, with manual review of suspected duplicates, resulting in 15,359 samples; (2) Validation excluding entries with corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and incorrect answers (approximately 10% discarded); (3) Categorization assigning problems to 13 predefined task categories based on source metadata; (4) Balanced sampling to equalize category representation, yielding 10,497 final samples.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Model responses were evaluated using a triadic evaluation system across three dimensions: (1) Content quality assessed by gpt-oss-20b using 13 task-specific evaluator prompts; (2) Speech quality measured by UTMOS; (3) Consistency between text and speech computed via modified Word Error Rate (WER) after transcribing speech outputs with Whisper-Large-v3. For role-play tasks, Wespeaker was used to calculate speaker similarity between model-generated speech and reference role audio. For emotion tasks, emotion2vec was used to obtain emotion probabilities.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A lightweight web-based curation tool was built to standardize quality checks. It ingests candidate items with metadata, raw prompts, reference answers, and associated media, and allows curators to assign Good or Bad verdicts with optional notes, exporting an audit log.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation was conducted on 10% of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B responses (1,050 examples) across all 13 tasks to validate the automated evaluation scheme. Pearson correlation coefficients between gpt-oss-20b scores and human ratings ranged from 0.73 to 1.00 (overall 0.92), and agreement rates were uniformly high (overall 96.1%). Evaluation stability was assessed by repeating scoring 10 times on 1,050 sampled examples, showing low variance across runs. Statistical significance testing using paired two-sided t-tests with Bonferroni correction was also performed.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The VoiceAssistant-Eval dataset and evaluation code will be publicly released under an MIT license. The authors bear responsibility in case of violation of rights. A data governance process for auditing and removal is maintained, with the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation using audio clips from 100 distinct roles (including 5 Chinese roles). The authors emphasize strict consent, provenance, and anti-impersonation safeguards, prohibiting training or releasing models intended to reproduce identifiable speakers without documented consent.
rai:dataSocialImpact: VoiceAssistant-Eval is intended to push the boundaries of AI assistant evaluation and guide development of next-generation multimodal models. The benchmark addresses safety alignment and robustness, with a dedicated safety task evaluating whether models refuse harmful requests. The authors note risks of misuse for identity spoofing, harassment, and fraud related to voice cloning, and require downstream users to implement consent gating and watermarking. The benchmark may facilitate development of voice assistants for healthcare, education, smart homes, customer service, and automotive applications.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark has a monolingual focus (English), with only five Chinese roles in the role-play task, which may not capture the full variability of real user interactions. Questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources, which might not reflect the full richness or fairness concerns of real deployments. The role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles that may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. The evaluation relies on automated measures and GPT-based scoring, which may introduce noise and bias, as the GPT judge may favor certain phrasings or overlook nuanced errors.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset (10.5K items) may be limited in diversity and has a monolingual (English) focus. The range of evaluated models is limited, with only one proprietary system (GPT-4o-Audio). The evaluation methodology relies on automated measures and GPT-based scoring. The benchmark does not cover video-audio integration, continuous audio-visual streaming, latency constraints, partial utterance handling, or barge-in scenarios. Evaluation is offline and static, not capturing real-time deployment factors. The dataset is not supposed to be used for training models for cheating.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for Testing and Evaluation of voice AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities. It is designed to benchmark open-source and proprietary models, identify gaps in robustness and safety alignment, and guide development of next-generation multimodal AI assistants. It is not intended for training models.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: gpt-oss-20b (content quality evaluation), UTMOS Strong / UTMOS (speech quality evaluation), Whisper-Large-v3 (speech transcription for consistency evaluation), emotion2vec (emotion probability estimation), Wespeaker (speaker similarity for role-play tasks), F5-TTS / ChatTTS / Dia-1.6B (speech synthesis), Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (text rewriting for TTS preprocessing)
